San Diego NDT under three rulebooks: Navy documents, NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A

San Diego aerospace NDT splits three ways. General Atomics Aeronautical Systems builds the MQ-9 and other unmanned aircraft in Poway, Northrop Grumman builds Global Hawk-family drones in Rancho Bernardo, and Collins Aerospace produces nacelles and aerostructures in Chula Vista. Fleet Readiness Center Southwest at Naval Air Station North Island overhauls Navy and Marine Corps aircraft. Around the bay, shipyards, a gas turbine maker and biotech plants employ technicians on quite different work. Before choosing a course, find out which of these worlds the job belongs to.

Poway, Rancho Bernardo and Chula Vista: aircraft and aerostructure makers

Aircraft and aerostructure manufacturers sit inside contracts that run from the customer to the prime and down to every supplier. Defense programs commonly carry NAS 410 down from the prime, since it replaced MIL-STD-410, and commercial airframe and engine customers write NAS 410 or EN 4179 into purchase-order quality clauses. Where such a clause applies, the employer certifies its inspectors under a NAS 410 written practice with a Responsible Level 3 (RL3) designated in writing, and Nadcap AC7114 audits the process at the site. An aerospace program built on SNT-TC-1A is possible where the customer's requirements allow it, but an SNT-TC-1A certificate can never answer a NAS 410 requirement. Machine and composite shops across the county see the same clauses one tier down.

North Island and the bay: Navy documents come first

Naval aviation maintenance at FRC Southwest follows Navy technical manuals, and the depot's own inspectors work under the Navy's directives, not under a private-sector scheme a candidate gets to choose. Ship work at General Dynamics NASSCO, BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair and their subcontractors follows NAVSEA technical publications that set their own personnel requirements. A contractor on Navy aviation work should read what its contract invokes: a Navy document, NAS 410 flowed down from a prime, or both.

Turbines, process plants and code work

Solar Turbines designs and builds industrial gas turbines in San Diego, and its castings, forgings and welded assemblies are examined against customer and in-house specifications; which personnel standard a turbine maker's written practice names is a question for its own Level 3. Biotech process equipment, power plants and structural steel follow ASME and AWS practice and an SNT-TC-1A written practice. A technician here can certify under SNT-TC-1A for years and meet NAS 410 only on moving to an aircraft maker or one of its suppliers.

Before you change sectors in San Diego

  • Ask which document, and which revision, the new written practice certifies to. NAS 410 Revision 6 came out in December 2025.
  • Bring course outlines and hour records. The RL3 credits evidence and may set gap training, most often in penetrant and magnetic particle, where NAS 410 wants more formal training than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  • Log experience by method and by product: airframe structure, castings, welds, composite panels.
  • Keep your examination results and vision records. The certification itself stays with the old employer.
  • Rehearse with the NDT practice tests before any general examination, whichever scheme it falls under.

For San Diego suppliers facing a customer or Nadcap audit

Shops serving both industrial and aerospace customers can run SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 programs side by side. State the standard and revision on every certification, keep training records to the stricter evidence standard, and apply the stricter vision and recertification rule wherever the two differ, so nobody ends up with two conflicting files. Atlantis offers NAS 410 audit documentation support in San Diego and aerospace Level III audit support; your RL3 keeps the approvals.

Atlantis for San Diego aerospace and aviation employers

Atlantis brings San Diego employers ASNT NDT Level III consulting, SNT-TC-1A-based training and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection, and aerospace and aviation companies are as much a part of that as shipyard contractors. Self-paced online theory comes with ASNT NDT Level III answers to questions, the Practical NDT simulator adds rehearsal, and the practical examination is held at the employer's facility; Atlantis has no San Diego classroom. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to San Diego companies or their technicians. Credit for outside training under a NAS 410 program is the RL3's decision, so get that answer before you enroll. See how NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A compare and the aviation NDT training page for more.
